Guide.title: Your guide to settling in Canada
Guide.subtitle: A simple, visual overview of what to know for your first weeks in Ottawa and Gatineau — summarized from official Canadian sources.
Guide.disclaimer: This guide is for general information only and summarizes public Canadian sources — it does not replace official information from IRCC, Service Canada, or your municipality, which may change.

transport.title: Transport from the airport
transport.body: From Ottawa's airport (YOW), the 97 express bus reaches downtown in about 30 minutes for $3.65. The O-Train light rail (Line 4) also connects the airport directly to downtown in 35-45 minutes.

steps.title: First steps
steps.body: As soon as you arrive: apply for your Social Insurance Number (SIN), register for provincial health insurance, and open a bank account. You can start working before your physical SIN arrives, as long as you've applied for one.

findUnit.title: Find a home
findUnit.body: Use our "Find a Home" page to filter available apartments by city, budget, bedrooms, and move-in date.

insurance.title: Tenant insurance
insurance.body: Tenant insurance isn't legally required, but most landlords require it as a lease condition. Expect about $15-30 per month — it covers your personal belongings and liability.

utilities.title: Internet / electricity
utilities.body: In Ottawa (Ontario), electricity is provided by Hydro Ottawa — set it up about 10 business days before you move in. In Gatineau (Quebec), Hydro-Québec serves your home.

bankAccount.title: Open a bank account
bankAccount.body: Canada's five major banks (RBC, TD, Scotiabank, BMO, CIBC) all offer newcomer packages: monthly fees are often waived for several months and no Canadian credit history is required.

payments.title: Understanding payments
payments.body: Card payments (Interac debit or credit) are used almost everywhere in Canada. Interac e-Transfer lets you send money instantly between Canadian bank accounts — handy for rent or splitting bills with roommates.

number.title: Getting a Canadian number
number.body: You can activate an eSIM before you even arrive to have a Canadian number the moment you land, or pick up a physical SIM card once you're here.

simPlan.title: Choosing a SIM card / plan
simPlan.body: Major carriers (Rogers, Bell, Telus) and their flanker brands (Fido, Koodo, Virgin Plus) offer newcomer plans with no Canadian credit check. Budget brands (Public Mobile, Lucky Mobile) work well on a tighter budget.

transit.title: Public transit
transit.body: A monthly OC Transpo pass (Ottawa) is also valid on the STO network (Gatineau) — you can cross the river without paying extra.

ottawaGatineau.title: Ottawa / Gatineau
ottawaGatineau.body: The two cities are connected by several bridges and an integrated bus network, making daily commutes between the two sides straightforward — even if you work on one side and live on the other.

checklist.title: Simple checklist
checklist.body: SIN, health card, bank account, phone plan, transit pass, monthly budget — then take time to connect with your new community: community centres, cultural associations, and settlement organizations like the YMCA-YWCA in Ottawa.
